FINDING / RELEASED: ordered decoder and exact observation space

I opened [PR1998](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1998), head9a3a967693055eba38ee4a5f5d311295fc4c224c, after rebasing onto current main51122344de9382e784c7f89953456d8cd55513ef. I release this scoped claim. The selected record remains unchanged.

The [proof and checker](https://github.com/jmbarrancoml/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9a3a967693055eba38ee4a5f5d311295fc4c224c/research/paired-log-ordered-decoder/README.md) give an explicit inverse for the nine-call paired-log controller. The equations preserve chart-operator order and restore all data and initial log blocks without an aggregate route-matrix inverse.

Given the final X banks and logs, the decoder uses precisely the four stacked observations `[R_(2j);R_(2j+1)]Y_j`. I prove that their kernel/row space equals the initial-log reconstruction space. Over a field the necessary and sufficient dimension is `sum_j rank([R_(2j);R_(2j+1)]) = 4r + sum_j rank(R_(2j)|ker R_(2j+1))`, between4r and8r. The ordered identity itself needs no field division. A finite cover/address realization must include its scalar multiplicity in r; this is not a rank over a presumed group-ring division field or a count of native children.

The registered Python3.12 replay passes after the rebase. It follows the pinned nineteen-event recipe, restores290 exact input columns, checks the complete observation row spaces, and rejects25 corruptions. Common, intermediate and noncommuting fixtures attain the expected query dimensions. Direct optimized Python3.14, source/metadata checks and diff-check also pass. These finite controls support the written proof; I claim no formal or independent human verification.

A useful obstruction within this interface is that the four initial odd-stage logs never reach final X or later logs. The two adjacent bridges cancel their propagation to the next pair, leaving their independent information in Y. A decoder using only FULL X/log streams therefore cannot restore the inputs. The proof identifies the remaining reads rather than pricing them as free.

Native query acquisition, Y-hole injections, routed ownership, precision and the complete recurrence invoice remain open. The theorem supplies scalar closure and the exact observation contract; it does not give an improved exponent.

Credit Zhihao Chen's retained PR377 implementation, Ali Romman's PR1862/1969 source and local-query work, Rohan Arun's PR1931 instances, and their predecessor lineage. I do not claim novelty for query swaps, triangular elimination or linear observability. Jose Manuel / @jmbarrancoml, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance and read-only mathematical agents.

FINDING / HANDOFF / RELEASED: limits of the common-hub terminal decoder

I finished this bounded investigation of the paired-log interface. I have no complete cheaper native decoder. I retain the selected exponent and release the claim with two obstructions and a corrected conditional budget.

**Fixed-route common-hub template.** Let `H_p=FULL*C_qp^-1`. For a requested old reader R_s, owner d reads port p at owner `d*rho_s(p)`. Ali Romman's [exact bridge review](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a6e6ad3936f67b8f63b5b68c5e75d540610a65e7/research/joint-query/evidence/BRIDGE-REVIEW.md) gives `rho_s(p)q_p=q_p`. After the prescribed owner reindexing, the source therefore has hole normal `d*q_p`; the remaining phase corrections are Paulis. The inverse injection route has the same property. This uses the complete affine inverse `M(g,delta)^*=M(g^-1,g^-1 delta)`.

For distinct ports, the binary symplectic B block of `H_r H_p^-1` is `q_p q_p^T+q_r q_r^T`, of rank two. Free monomial wrappers preserve this rank. For any common query frame Q, summing triangle inequalities over the 104 non-A ports gives

`sum_p distance(H_p,Q) >= 104`.

The same inequality holds for a common injection frame S. Thus a decoder that transports each non-A field to a common frame before gathering, then transports each correction from a common frame, needs at least **208 rank units per bank**, or **832 across four banks**. I grant the A-port and log work free in this bound. I checked the fixed-route premises on all 1,008 pinned port-stage charts and all 6,216 distinct port pairs. I leave joint mutable-data circuits, row-specific frames and changed controllers open.

For the nine-stage dedicated-log model, I obtain deficit 824 before decoding, so I cannot obtain positive coverage with this template. For an odd-stage variant with the same hosted coverage law, v ports, r selected ports and s calls, I obtain deficit `(s-1)v-sr` and a two-leg common-hub bill of at least `(s-1)(v-r)`. Their difference is `-r`. A researcher must change another hypothesis to obtain positive coverage with this template.

The apparent one-way shortcut also changes the endpoint. After lifting Y to FULL and decoding, one must still account for the original X input encoding C_q. The retained endpoint is `FULL*C_q^-1`; relative to the X input frame C_q, it gives `FULL*C_q^-2`, a Pauli correction of FULL. Omitting the return line applications loses this identity.

**One extra future chart does not supply the old reader.** Add an unused E9 block and let R9 denote its aligned reader. On payload-constant fields with arbitrary cover values, choose

`h = (56I - R9^* R9) R_s^* e`.

Since `R9 R9^*=56I`, we have `R9 h=0`. I checked that the 112 owner words `rho_s(p)rho_9(p)` are distinct for each old stage s=0,...,8. Writing r_p for a column of R, we have `sum r_p r_p^T=56I` and `r_p^T r_p=4`. We therefore obtain the identity-cover coefficient of `R_s h`:

CLAIM: averaged-rank bound for the paired-log phase-query primitive

I will verify and document a lower bound for the proposed matched terminal query swap. Base main: `e112d71c8d7bb32435debcc54df932593dd8223a`. I build on Ali Romman's native source codes and phase conventions, Rohan Arun's #1931 local words, my #1998 ordered decoder, and the scoped common-hub finding [18930295](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1167#discussioncomment-18930295).

Changed hypothesis: I allow off-frame physical scalar mixing, COPY, CLEAR, clean ancillas and discarded temporaries. I retain a fixed linear schedule, single-array commuting convolution-phase children and uniform tensor-power Paulis. I will construct a common Pauli-trivial character sector before applying the rank argument; the unrestricted statement would fail on a free Pauli target.

The proposed lemma is `k >= (2/3)(d_image + d_row - average_rank)`, with the dimensions taken from target differences against the all-queries-identity baseline. I derive it through a strictly causal query expansion and Sylvester's inequality. I credit eumemic's #288 compact-WY, image/row-span and character arguments and Ali Romman's #468 factorization as predecessors.

For the coherent matched P112 target, I obtain candidate dimensions112 on each side and character defect rank at most16. Four independent targets would then require at least555 phase calls even with shared linear workspace, exceeding the declared conditional terminal budget. I will check the actual source minor, the character-sector construction, singular-workspace examples and the target rank identities before making that conclusion public as a result.

This scope excludes noncommuting payload-coordinate adapters, nonlinear intermediate operations and joint multirole child interfaces. I do not identify the full mixed-chart ordered decoder with this matched target without a separate proof. I retain the selected frontier.

Expected artifact: a proof, exact replay with failure controls, and a focused PR if the checks hold. Claim expires: 2026-10-14 20:25 UTC. I use substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.
